paper.title: Data-Dependent Regret Bounds for Constrained MABs

settings.name_in_paper: Constrained MAB with adversarial losses and stochastic constraints, soft constraints
unmapped: m unknown stochastic constraint costs in [0,1]^K drawn i.i.d. from unknown distributions, observed for the played arm; thresholds alpha_i known
regret measured against the best fixed randomized strategy satisfying the constraints in expectation
learner knows the cumulative loss of the constrained optimal strategy sum_t l_t^T x* (to tune eta; removable via doubling trick per the paper)
settings.definition_quote: we focus on constrained MAB problems in which the losses are chosen adversarially and the constraint costs are selected stochastically ... the loss vector \lvec_t is chosen by an adaptive adversary ... V_T := max_i sum_t [g_i^T x_t - alpha_i]^+ ... The goal is to guarantee that V_T = o(T).

settings.name_in_paper: Constrained MAB with adversarial losses and stochastic constraints, hard constraints
unmapped: m unknown stochastic constraint costs in [0,1]^K drawn i.i.d., observed for played arm; thresholds alpha_i known
Slater's condition; learner knows the max-margin strictly feasible strategy x^diamond, its costs theta_i and margin rho
learner knows sum_t l_t^T x* to tune eta
regret measured against best fixed randomized strategy satisfying constraints in expectation
settings.definition_quote: In this setting, the goal of the learner is to guarantee that g_i^T x_t <= alpha_i for every constraint i in [m] and round t in [T] with high probability. ... Assumption 1 (Slater's condition) ... Assumption 2 (Knowledge of a strictly feasible strategy)

settings.name_in_paper: Constrained MAB with hard constraints (lower bound)
unmapped: m stochastic constraint costs with known thresholds; strictly feasible strategy x^diamond with margin rho
worst case over constrained small-loss ball B_{omega,Delta,T}
settings.definition_quote: We define the constrained small-loss balls as B_{omega,Delta,T} := { l_{1:T} in [0,1]^{KT} : sum_t l_t^T x*/T <= omega and sum_t (l_t^T(x^diamond - x*))^2/T <= Delta^2 }.

source.label: thm:viol
source.quote: Let $\delta \in (0,1)$. Then, with probability at least $1-2\delta$, the \algnamesoft algorithm suffers cumulative positive constraint violations $V_T \le \mathcal{O}\left( \sqrt{KT\ln\left(\nicefrac{TKm}{\delta}\right)} \right).$

results.notes: Bound on cumulative positive constraint violation V_T, not regret; probability 1-2delta. Paper's m is number of constraints (not combinatorial size), renamed m_c.

symbols.L_xstar: cumulative loss sum_t l_t^T x* of the optimal constrained (randomized) strategy

tuning: eta = min{1/(40 H ln T ln(H/delta)), sqrt(K/(L_xstar ln(1/delta)))}, H = ln(ceil(ln T) ceil(3 ln T)/delta)

source.label: thm:reg_soft
source.quote: Let $\delta \in (0,1)$ and $\eta= \min\{...\}$ ... Then, with probability at least $1-4\delta$, \algnamesoft suffers a cumulative regret bounded as $R_T(\lvec_{1:T}) \le \widetilde{\mathcal{O}}\left( \sqrt{K\sum_{t=1}^{T}\lvec_t^\top\xvec^* \ln\left(\nicefrac{1}{\delta}\right)}\right).$

results.notes: Probability 1-4delta. Regret uses actual losses l_t^T x_t (adaptive adversary). Tuning requires knowledge of L_xstar.

symbols.rho: Slater margin of the known strictly feasible strategy x^diamond
symbols.L_xstar: cumulative loss sum_t l_t^T x* of the optimal constrained strategy

conditions: Slater's condition; x^diamond and its costs known (Assumption 2)
tuning: eta = min{rho/(40 H ln T ln(H/delta)), sqrt(K/(L_xstar ln(1/delta)))}, H = ln(ceil(ln T) ceil(3 ln T)/delta)

source.label: thr:ub_hard
source.quote: Let $\delta\in(0,1)$, $\rho\geq \frac{12K}{T}$, and $\eta= \min\{...\}$ ... Then, \algnamehard suffers a cumulative regret bounded as: $R_T(\lvec_{1:T})\leq \widetilde{\mathcal{O}}( \frac{K\ln (1/\delta)}{\rho}\sqrt{\sum_{t=1}^T(\lvec_t^\top(\xvec^\diamond - \xvec^*))^2}+\frac{1}{\rho}\sqrt{K\sum_{t=1}^{T}\lvec_t^\top\xvec^* \ln(\frac{1}{\delta})})$

results.notes: Theorem statement omits the probability; proof states it holds w.p. at least 1-5delta. Õ hides logs not depending on delta. Also, Theorem (thm:safety) guarantees constraints satisfied every round w.p. 1-delta.

symbols.Delta_ball: paper's Delta: bound on root-mean-square of l_t^T(x^diamond - x*) over the small-loss ball
symbols.omega: bound on average loss of x* over the small-loss ball

conditions: sup over loss sequences in B_{omega,Delta,T}

source.quote: For all $ \omega \in [0,1]$ and for all $ \Delta \in [0,1]$, it holds $\sup_{\lvec_{1:T} \in \mathcal{B}_{\omega,\Delta, T}} \mathbb{E}[R_T(\lvec_{1:T})] \le \widetilde{\mathcal{O}}\left(\frac{K\Delta}{\rho}\sqrt{T}+ \frac{1}{\rho} \sqrt{K\omega T}\right)$

results.notes: Expectation over the algorithm's internal randomization of R_T defined via l_t^T x_t, i.e. regret against fixed constrained strategy for a given loss sequence; mapped to expected_regret.

symbols.Delta_ball: paper's Delta: RMS of l_t^T(x^diamond - x*) bound defining the ball
symbols.omega: bound on average loss of x* over the ball

conditions: sup over loss sequences in B_{omega,Delta,T}
algorithm must satisfy hard constraints with high probability (proof uses delta < 1/2)

source.label: thr:lb
source.quote: Let $K\ge 2$, $T \ge \max\left\{2, (11+\ln T)\left(\frac{8}{3}\right)^2\right\}$, and $\omega \in \left[\frac{1}{T}\left(\frac{11}{2}+\ln T\right), \frac{1}{2}\right]$. Then for every randomized algorithm, we have $\sup_{\lvec_{1:T} \in \mathcal{B}_{\omega,\Delta, T}} \mathbb{E}[R_T(\lvec_{1:T})] \ge \Omega\left(\frac{\Delta}{\rho}\sqrt{T}+  \sqrt{\omega T}\right)$

results.notes: Construction uses K=3 instances with stochastic Bernoulli losses and constraints; the class of algorithms is those safe with high probability. Explicit constants in proof: 9/1024 sqrt(T omega) + Delta sqrt(T)/(48 rho).
